To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel protein, p51-Nedasin, is a novel NE-dlig/SAP102 binding protein and interferes with the NE-dlg/SAPI102-NMDA receptor interaction in vitro.
a novel protein, p51-Nedasin, was identified as a binding partner of NE-dlg/Sap102 and that Nedasin may interfere with the association between Sap102 and NMDAR2B.
we identified p51-nedesin, a novel MAGUK-interacting protein that is involved in the formation of synapses during neuronal cell differentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of the novel NE-dlg-associated protein, p 51-nedasin and the elucidation of the role of the protein in the formation of synapse.
the isolation of a protein that interferes with the binding between NE-dlg and NMDA receptors and its possible involvement in the formation of postsynaptic density.
the identification of a novel NE-Dlg-associated protein, pS1-nedasin, which is expressed in the cell body, and the elucidation of the function of this protein in the neuronal cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nedasin is an endogenous inhibitor for the interaction of NE-dlg/Sap102 with the NMDA receptor.
nedasin is a novel NE-dlag/SAP102-associated amidohydrolasesuperfamily protein that may be implicated in synapse formation and function.
nedasin is a novel protein that interferes with NE-dlg-mediated clustering of NMDA receptor in neuronal cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NE-dlg/SAG102 is a key molecule for clustering of the NMDA receptor at the synapses and nedasin is a negative regulator for the function of NE-dlg/SAPI102.
the NE-dlg/Sap102-associated protein, nedasin, interferes with the interaction between NE-dlg and NMDA-R2B.
the alternative splice variant of nedasin may be a novel factor involved in the formation of synapses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of nedasin is increased in parallel with the formation of synapses, and it co-localizes mainly in cell bodies with NE-dlg, a protein that is known to interact with NMDA receptors.
the alternative splicing of the p51-nedasain gene produces four variants, S, V1, v2, and V1, which differ in the carboxyl terminus, and that the S form is predominantly expressed in the brain.

nedasin is an important factor in the formation and structural change of synapses during neuronal differentiation and that it plays an important role in the clustering of neurotransmitter receptor molecules at the synaptic site by interfering with the binding between the NMDA receptor and NE-dlg/SAPT02.
